blocks.text: O'zbekchada javobda fe'l takrorlanadi: «Tugatdingmi? — Ha, **tugatdim**». Ingliz tilida esa fe'l va undan keyingi qism takrorlanmaydi — o'rniga faqat **yordamchi fe'l** qoladi: Have you finished? — Yes, I **have**. Agar gapda yordamchi fe'l bo'lmasa (Present / Past Simple), **do / does / did** ishlatiladi. Qisqa javoblar va too / either qizil kitobda o'tilgan (→ qizil kitob, 40–42-darslar); bu darsda — urg'uli yordamchi fe'l, qayta so'roq, So do I / Neither can I ning nozik joylari va I think so / I hope not.

rows: We haven't been to Khiva, but our parents **have**.
I can't swim, but my sister **can**.
She doesn't eat meat, but her husband **does**.

blocks.text: Urg'u bilan: I DO like it — «rostdan ham»

Yordamchi fe'lni urg'u bilan aytsak, u qarshi fikrni rad etadi yoki ta'kidlaydi: You don't like plov. — I **do** like it! Darak gapda yordamchi fe'l bo'lmasa, ta'kid uchun **do / does / did** qo'shiladi: I **did** tell you! (Aytgandim-ku!). O'zbekchada bunga «**-ku**», «**rostdan ham**», «**haqiqatan**» to'g'ri keladi. Buyruq gapda ham bor: **Do** sit down! — O'tiring-da!

items.text: I **do** like your new haircut — honestly!
items.translation: Yangi soch turmagingiz menga **rostdan yoqdi** — chin dildan!

items.text: You **did** promise to help me with the move!

blocks.text: Qayta so'roq: Have you? Did it? — qiziqish va hayrat

Suhbatdoshning gapiga **yordamchi fe'l + olmosh** bilan javob berish (reply question) — haqiqiy savol emas, balki qiziqish, hayrat yoki tinglayotganingizni ko'rsatish: I've just got engaged. — Oh, **have you**? Congratulations! Gap inkor bo'lsa, qayta so'roq ham inkor: I don't eat sugar. — **Don't you**? O'zbekchada bunga «**Shunaqami?**», «**Rostdanmi?**» yoki fe'lning o'zi + -mi to'g'ri keladi: «Yemaydimi?»

items.text: I've lost my job. — Oh, **have you**? I'm so sorry.
It was minus twenty in Moscow last week. — **Was it**?
items.translation: O'tgan hafta Moskvada minus yigirma edi. — **Rostdanmi**?

items.text: Aziz doesn't like football. — **Doesn't he**? I'm surprised.

blocks.text: So do I / Neither can I

O'zbekchadagi bitta «**Men ham**» inglizchada ikkiga bo'linadi: ijobiy gapga — **So + yordamchi fe'l + ega** (So am I, So do I), inkor gapga — **Neither / Nor + yordamchi fe'l + ega** (Neither can I, Nor did we). Yordamchi fe'l zamon va shaklga mos bo'lishi shart: I went → So **did** I; I've seen → So **have** I. So'zlashuvda: **Me too** / **Me neither**. Rozi bo'lmasangiz — oddiy qisqa javob: I love winter. — Oh, **I don't**.

items.text: I'm starving. — **So am I**. Let's get something to eat.
items.translation: Qornim juda och. — **Meniki ham**. Biror narsa yeylik.

items.text: I haven't seen the new film yet. — **Neither have I**.
I really like jazz. — Oh, **I don't**. It's too slow for me.
items.translation: Jazni juda yaxshi ko'raman. — **Men unchalik emas**. Men uchun juda sekin.

blocks.text: So'z tartibiga e'tibor bering: **So do I** — «men ham». **So I do** (ega oldin) — butunlay boshqa ma'no: «ha, rostdan ham shunday ekan» (kutilmagan faktni tan olish): You've left the lights on. — **So I have**! — Chiroqni yoqib qoldiribsan. — **Ha-ya, rostdan**!
I think so / I hope not

think, hope, expect, suppose, guess va be afraid dan keyin butun gapni takrorlamaslik uchun **so** (ijobiy) yoki **not** (inkor) ishlatiladi: Is she coming? — **I think so**. Inkor shakllar turlicha: **I don't think so** (I think not — juda rasmiy), **I hope not** («I don't hope so» — xato!), **I'm afraid not**, **I don't expect so / I expect not**, **I suppose not / I don't suppose so**. **I'm afraid so / not** — noxush xabarni muloyim yetkazish.

O'zbeklarning tipik xatolari: inkor gapga «Me too» → **Me neither** / **Neither do I**; «Neither I can» → **Neither can I** (tartib: yordamchi fe'l, keyin ega); «So I do» (= men ham) → **So do I**; «I don't hope so» → **I hope not**; «I think yes / I think no» → **I think so** / **I don't think so**; «Do you like it? — Yes, I like» → Yes, I **do**; zamon mos kelmasligi: «I saw it. — So do I» → **So did I**.

«Men ham» deyishdan oldin oldingi gapdagi yordamchi fe'lni toping (am, have, can, did ...) va uni **So / Neither** dan keyin qo'ying. Yordamchi fe'l ko'rinmasa — **do / does / did**. Gap inkor bo'lsa — **Neither**, ijobiy bo'lsa — **So**.

rows: Ta'kid: urg'uli yordamchi fe'l / do, did
Rozi: So / Neither + yordamchi fe'l + ega
**I think so**. **I hope not**. **I'm afraid so**.

examples.title: Avoiding repetition: **I haven't**, but Jasur **has**
examples.description: Fe'l takrorlanmaydi — faqat yordamchi fe'l qoladi: qisqa javoblar va «men emas, lekin u» qarama-qarshiligi.

sentences.text: Have you ever been to Edinburgh? — No, I **haven't**, but my brother **has**.
sentences.translation: Edinburgda hech bo'lganmisiz? — Yo'q, men **bo'lmaganman**, lekin akam **bo'lgan**.

sentences.text: Madina doesn't drink coffee, but her husband **does** — about five cups a day.
sentences.translation: Madina qahva ichmaydi, eri esa **ichadi** — kuniga beshtacha piyola.

sentences.text: I wasn't invited to the meeting, but all my colleagues **were**.
sentences.translation: Meni yig'ilishga taklif qilishmadi, hamma hamkasblarimni esa **taklif qilishdi**.

sentences.text: Can you speak Korean? — I **can't**, but I'd love to learn.
sentences.translation: Koreyscha gapira olasizmi? — **Gapira olmayman**, lekin o'rganishni juda xohlardim.

sentences.text: Jasur said he would call me, and he **did** — at six in the morning!
sentences.translation: Jasur menga qo'ng'iroq qilishini aytgan edi, **qildi** ham — ertalab soat oltida!

sentences.text: Aren't you tired after the flight? — I **am** a bit, but I'm too excited to sleep.
sentences.translation: Parvozdan keyin charchamadingizmi? — Biroz **charchadim**, lekin uxlash uchun juda hayajondaman.

sentences.text: Most of my friends have already got married, but I **haven't** yet.
sentences.translation: Do'stlarimning ko'pi allaqachon turmush qurgan, men esa hali **qurmaganman**.

sentences.text: Did you lock the car? — I think I **did**, but let me check.
sentences.translation: Mashinani qulfladingmi? — **Qulflagan** bo'lsam kerak, lekin tekshirib ko'ray.

sentences.text: Sarah will probably come to the party, but James **won't** — he's working.
sentences.translation: Sara ziyofatga kelsa kerak, lekin Jeyms **kelmaydi** — u ishlayapti.

sentences.text: You should apologise to her. — I know I **should**, but it's hard.
sentences.translation: Undan kechirim so'rashing kerak. — Bilaman, **so'rashim kerak**, lekin qiyin.

examples.title: Emphasis: I **do** like it! I **did** tell you!
examples.description: Urg'uli yordamchi fe'l — qarshi fikrni rad etish yoki ta'kidlash. Darak gapda do / does / did qo'shiladi. O'zbekchada «-ku», «rostdan ham».

sentences.text: You never eat my plov! — That's not true — I **do** eat it, just not every day.
sentences.translation: Mening palovimni hech yemaysan! — Bu noto'g'ri — **yeyman-ku**, faqat har kuni emas.

sentences.text: I **did** tell you about the meeting — you just weren't listening.
sentences.translation: Yig'ilish haqida senga **aytgandim-ku** — sen shunchaki eshitmagansan.

sentences.text: Bekzod **does** work hard; he just doesn't show it.
sentences.translation: Bekzod **haqiqatan ham** qattiq ishlaydi, faqat buni ko'rsatmaydi.

sentences.text: I'm sure you've forgotten my birthday. — I **haven't**! Your present is in the car.
sentences.translation: Tug'ilgan kunimni unutgansan, aniq. — **Unutganim yo'q**! Sovg'ang mashinada.

sentences.text: We **did** enjoy the trip, even though it rained every day.
sentences.translation: Har kuni yomg'ir yog'gan bo'lsa ham, sayohat bizga **rostdan yoqdi**.

sentences.text: **Do** sit down — you've been standing for an hour.
sentences.translation: **O'tiring-da** — bir soatdan beri tik turibsiz.

sentences.text: I know you don't believe me, but I **am** telling the truth!
sentences.translation: Menga ishonmasligingni bilaman, lekin men **rostini aytyapman**!

sentences.text: She doesn't look sixty, but she really **is**.
sentences.translation: U oltmish yoshda ko'rinmaydi, lekin rostdan **oltmishda**.

sentences.text: Kate thought nobody would come, but in the end lots of people **did**.
sentences.translation: Keyt hech kim kelmaydi deb o'ylagan edi, lekin oxirida ko'p odam **keldi**.

sentences.text: If you **do** decide to move to London, let me know.
sentences.translation: Agar Londonga ko'chishga **rostdan qaror qilsangiz**, menga xabar bering.

examples.title: Reply questions: **Have you?** **Did it?** **Doesn't she?**
examples.description: Qayta so'roq — qiziqish yoki hayrat: yordamchi fe'l + olmosh. O'zbekchada «Shunaqami?», «Rostdanmi?» yoki fe'l + -mi.

sentences.text: I've just been offered a job in Dubai. — **Have you**? That's fantastic news!
sentences.translation: Menga hozirgina Dubayda ish taklif qilishdi. — **Rostdanmi**? Bu ajoyib yangilik!

sentences.text: It snowed in Tashkent last night. — **Did it**? I didn't notice anything.
sentences.translation: Kecha Toshkentda qor yog'di. — **Shunaqami**? Hech narsani sezmabman.

sentences.text: Madina doesn't eat bread at all. — **Doesn't she**? How strange.
sentences.translation: Madina umuman non yemaydi. — **Yemaydimi**? G'alati-ku.

sentences.text: Tom can speak five languages. — **Can he**? Which ones?
sentences.translation: Tom beshta tilda gapira oladi. — **Gapira oladimi**? Qaysilarida?

sentences.text: We're moving to Samarkand next month. — Oh, **are you**? Why?
sentences.translation: Kelasi oy Samarqandga ko'chyapmiz. — **Ko'chyapsizlarmi**? Nega?

sentences.text: I won't be at the party on Saturday. — **Won't you**? What a pity!
sentences.translation: Shanba kuni ziyofatda bo'lmayman. — **Bo'lmaysanmi**? Attang!

sentences.text: This laptop was only fifty pounds at the market. — **Was it**? It looks much more expensive.
sentences.translation: Bu noutbuk bozorda bor-yo'g'i ellik funt edi. — **Shunaqami**? Ancha qimmatroq ko'rinadi.

sentences.text: My parents have never been abroad. — **Haven't they**? Not even to Turkey?
sentences.translation: Ota-onam hech qachon chet elga chiqmagan. — **Chiqmaganmi**? Hatto Turkiyaga ham?

sentences.text: Aziz is getting married in June. — **Is he**? Who to?
sentences.translation: Aziz iyunda uylanyapti. — **Uylanyaptimi**? Kimga?

sentences.text: I'd rather stay at home tonight. — **Would you**? But it's your birthday!
sentences.translation: Bugun kechqurun uyda qolganim ma'qul. — **Qolmoqchimisan**? Axir bugun tug'ilgan kuning-ku!

examples.title: **So do I** / **So was I** / **So have I**
examples.description: Ijobiy gapga rozilik: So + yordamchi fe'l + ega. Yordamchi fe'l oldingi gapdagi zamonga mos keladi.

sentences.text: I love walking in the mountains. — **So do I**. Let's go to Chimgan on Sunday.
sentences.translation: Tog'da sayr qilishni yaxshi ko'raman. — **Men ham**. Yakshanba kuni Chimyonga boraylik.

sentences.text: I was really nervous before the exam. — **So was I**, but it was easier than I expected.
sentences.translation: Imtihondan oldin juda hayajonlangan edim. — **Men ham**, lekin kutganimdan osonroq bo'ldi.

sentences.text: Kate has applied for the job in Oxford, and **so has** her sister.
sentences.translation: Keyt Oksforddagi ishga hujjat topshirdi, singlisi **ham**.

sentences.text: We're going to the concert tonight. — **So are we**! Maybe we'll see you there.
sentences.translation: Bugun kechqurun konsertga boramiz. — **Biz ham**! Balki u yerda ko'rishib qolarmiz.

sentences.text: Aziz passed his driving test first time, and **so did** his twin brother.
sentences.translation: Aziz haydovchilik imtihonidan birinchi urinishda o'tdi, egizak akasi **ham**.

sentences.text: Ideally, I'd like to live by the sea one day. — **So would I**, but I can't afford it.
sentences.translation: Bir kun dengiz bo'yida yashashni xohlardim. — **Men ham**, lekin bunga pulim yetmaydi.

sentences.text: My phone battery is almost dead. — **So is mine**. Is there a charger anywhere?
sentences.translation: Telefonimning quvvati deyarli tugadi. — **Meniki ham**. Biror joyda zaryadlovchi bormi?

sentences.text: Dilnoza can play the piano beautifully, and **so can** her daughter.
sentences.translation: Dilnoza pianinoni chiroyli chaladi, qizi **ham**.

sentences.text: I've been to Bukhara three times. — **So have I** — it's my favourite city.
sentences.translation: Buxoroda uch marta bo'lganman. — **Men ham** — bu mening eng sevimli shahrim.

sentences.text: When the lights went out, the children screamed, and **so did** some of the adults.
sentences.translation: Chiroq o'chganda bolalar qichqirib yubordi, ba'zi kattalar **ham**.

examples.title: **Neither can I** / **Nor did we** / **Me neither**
examples.description: Inkor gapga rozilik: Neither / Nor + yordamchi fe'l + ega; so'zlashuvda Me neither. O'zbekchada baribir «men ham».

sentences.text: I can't stand horror films. — **Neither can I**. Let's watch a comedy.
sentences.translation: Qo'rqinchli filmlarni ko'rolmayman. — **Men ham**. Komediya ko'raylik.

sentences.text: Honestly, I didn't understand a word of that lecture. — **Neither did I**!
sentences.translation: Rostini aytsam, o'sha ma'ruzadan bir og'iz ham tushunmadim. — **Men ham**!

sentences.text: Jasur hasn't finished his project yet, and **neither has** Bekzod.
sentences.translation: Jasur loyihasini hali tugatmadi, Bekzod **ham**.

sentences.text: We weren't told about the changes. — **Nor were we**. Nobody tells us anything.
sentences.translation: Bizga o'zgarishlar haqida aytishmadi. — **Bizga ham**. Hech kim bizga hech narsa aytmaydi.

sentences.text: My parents don't use social media, and **neither do** my grandparents, of course.
sentences.translation: Ota-onam ijtimoiy tarmoqlardan foydalanmaydi, bobo-buvim **ham**, albatta.

sentences.text: I'm not very good at maths. — **Me neither** — that's why I chose languages.
sentences.translation: Matematikadan unchalik yaxshi emasman. — **Men ham** — shuning uchun tillarni tanladim.

sentences.text: Emma won't be at work tomorrow, and **neither will** James — they're both at a conference.
sentences.translation: Emma ertaga ishda bo'lmaydi, Jeyms **ham** — ikkalasi ham konferensiyada.

sentences.text: I've never tried sushi. — **Neither have I**, but I'd like to.
sentences.translation: Hech qachon sushi tatib ko'rmaganman. — **Men ham**, lekin tatib ko'rmoqchiman.

sentences.text: Our neighbours couldn't sleep because of the storm, and **nor could** we.
sentences.translation: Qo'shnilarimiz bo'ron tufayli uxlay olmadi, **biz ham**.

sentences.text: Nilufar doesn't like flying. — **Neither does** her husband, so they always take the train.
sentences.translation: Nilufar samolyotda uchishni yoqtirmaydi. — Eri **ham**, shuning uchun ular doim poyezdda yurishadi.

examples.title: Agree or disagree: **So are we!** / **Oh, I don't.**
examples.description: Rozi bo'lsak — So / Neither, rozi bo'lmasak — oddiy qisqa javob (I don't, I am, I did). Ko'pincha qayta so'roq bilan birga.

sentences.text: I love living in a big city. — Oh, **I don't**. I'd prefer a quiet village.
sentences.translation: Katta shaharda yashashni yaxshi ko'raman. — Men esa **yoqtirmayman**. Tinch qishloqni afzal ko'raman.

sentences.text: I'm not tired at all. — Really? **I am**. I could sleep for a week.
sentences.translation: Umuman charchamadim. — Rostdanmi? **Men charchadim**. Bir hafta uxlasam ham bo'ladi.

sentences.text: Personally, I didn't enjoy the film much. — **Didn't you**? **I did**.
sentences.translation: Shaxsan menga film unchalik yoqmadi. — **Yoqmadimi**? **Menga yoqdi**.

sentences.text: Kate has already booked her holiday. — Lucky her! **I haven't** even started looking.
sentences.translation: Keyt allaqachon ta'tilini band qilib qo'ydi. — Omadi bor ekan! Men hali qidirishni ham **boshlamadim**.

sentences.text: Since I can't drive, I'll take the bus. — No need — **I can**, so I'll give you a lift.
sentences.translation: Mashina hayday olmaganim uchun avtobusda ketaman. — Shart emas — **men hayday olaman**, seni olib ketaman.

sentences.text: Most of my friends liked the new teacher, but **I didn't**.
sentences.translation: Do'stlarimning ko'piga yangi o'qituvchi yoqdi, lekin **menga yoqmadi**.

sentences.text: We're going to Khiva for the holidays. — **So are we**! Which hotel are you staying at?
sentences.translation: Ta'tilda Xivaga boryapmiz. — **Biz ham**! Qaysi mehmonxonada qolasizlar?

sentences.text: I wouldn't like to work at night. — **Wouldn't you**? **I would** — the pay is much better.
sentences.translation: Kechasi ishlashni xohlamasdim. — **Xohlamasmiding**? **Men xohlardim** — maoshi ancha yaxshi.

sentences.text: My sister hates cooking, and **so does** my mother, so my dad does it all.
sentences.translation: Opam ovqat pishirishni yomon ko'radi, onam **ham**, shuning uchun hammasini dadam qiladi.

sentences.text: Aziz thinks the plan will work, but **I don't** — it's far too risky.
sentences.translation: Aziz reja ishlaydi deb o'ylaydi, lekin **men unday o'ylamayman** — juda xavfli.

examples.title: **I think so** / **I hope not** / **I'm afraid so**
examples.description: Butun gapni takrorlamaslik: think / hope / expect / suppose / guess / be afraid + so yoki not. «I don't hope so» deyilmaydi.

sentences.text: Is the museum open on Mondays? — **I don't think so**. Let's check online.
sentences.translation: Muzey dushanba kunlari ochiqmi? — **Menimcha, yo'q**. Internetdan tekshiraylik.

sentences.text: Will it rain tomorrow? — **I hope not** — we're having a picnic.
sentences.translation: Ertaga yomg'ir yog'adimi? — **Yog'masin-da** — piknik qilmoqchimiz.

sentences.text: Is Jasur coming to the wedding? — **I expect so**; he never misses a party.
sentences.translation: Jasur to'yga keladimi? — **Kelsa kerak**, u hech qachon bazmni qoldirmaydi.

sentences.text: Have we missed the last bus? — **I'm afraid so**. We'll have to get a taxi.
sentences.translation: Oxirgi avtobusdan qoldikmi? — **Afsuski, ha**. Taksi olishga to'g'ri keladi.

sentences.text: Can I pay by card here? — **I'm afraid not**, only cash.
sentences.translation: Bu yerda karta bilan to'lasam bo'ladimi? — **Afsuski, yo'q**, faqat naqd pul.

sentences.text: Do you think Madina will get the job? — **I hope so**. She really deserves it.
sentences.translation: Sizningcha, Madina ishga olinadimi? — **Umid qilaman**. U bunga chindan loyiq.

sentences.text: Shall we invite Bekzod as well? — **I suppose so**, although he's always late.
sentences.translation: Bekzodni ham taklif qilamizmi? — **Mayli-ya**, garchi u doim kechiksa ham.

sentences.text: Has the price gone up again? — **I guess so** — everything's more expensive these days.
sentences.translation: Narx yana oshdimi? — **Shunday shekilli** — bugungi kunda hamma narsa qimmatroq.

sentences.text: Will the meeting last long? — **I shouldn't think so**; there are only two points on the agenda.
sentences.translation: Yig'ilish uzoq davom etadimi? — **Unchalik emas, menimcha**; kun tartibida faqat ikkita masala bor.

sentences.text: Are we going to be late? — **I don't expect so**, if the traffic isn't too bad.
sentences.translation: Kechikamizmi? — **Kechikmasak kerak**, agar tirbandlik unchalik bo'lmasa.

examples.title: Dialogue: planning a weekend in the mountains
examples.description: Ikki do'st dam olish kunlarini rejalashtiradi: ta'kidli do, So do I, qayta so'roq, Neither can I, I think so, I suppose so.

sentences.text: — I'm so tired of the city — I really **do** need a break this weekend.
sentences.translation: — Shahardan juda charchadim — bu dam olish kunlari menga dam **rostdan ham** kerak.

sentences.text: — **So do I**! Why don't we go to Chimgan on Saturday?
sentences.translation: — **Menga ham**! Shanba kuni Chimyonga bormaymizmi?

sentences.text: — Good idea, but **will** the road be open after all that snow?
sentences.translation: — Yaxshi fikr, lekin shuncha qordan keyin yo'l **ochiq bo'ladimi**?

sentences.text: — **I think so**. My cousin drove up there yesterday, and he was fine.
sentences.translation: — **Menimcha, ha**. Amakivachcham kecha u yerga mashinada borgan, hech qanday muammo bo'lmagan.

sentences.text: — Oh, **did he**? Then let's go. Can you drive, though? I can't.
sentences.translation: — **Shunaqami**? Unda boraylik. Lekin sen hayday olasanmi? Men olmayman.

sentences.text: — **Neither can I**, but Aziz **can**, and he's free on Saturday.
sentences.translation: — **Men ham**, lekin Aziz **hayday oladi**, u shanba kuni bo'sh.

sentences.text: — **Is he**? I thought he was working this weekend.
sentences.translation: — **Bo'shmi**? Bu dam olish kunlari ishlaydi deb o'ylagandim.

sentences.text: — He **was**, but his plans changed. Will he mind driving us, do you think?
sentences.translation: — **Ishlashi kerak edi**, lekin rejasi o'zgardi. Bizni olib borishga qarshilik qilmasmikan?

sentences.text: — **I don't think so** — he loves driving. Shall we leave at seven?
sentences.translation: — **Menimcha, yo'q** — u mashina haydashni yaxshi ko'radi. Soat yettida chiqamizmi?

sentences.text: — Fine, **I suppose so**, although I'd rather sleep a bit longer!
sentences.translation: — Mayli, **shunday qila qolaylik**, garchi biroz ko'proq uxlashni afzal ko'rsam ham!
